name: Yen & carry trade
summary: Yen near ¥158.8 per dollar on 11 Nov, little changed on the week and month; no intervention reported
state: The dollar was near ¥158.8 early on 11 Nov, up 0.3% on both the week and the month, far inside the 3% weekly and 6% monthly Watch lines (Yahoo Finance). The yen is about 3% stronger than its 52-week low of ¥163.9 per dollar. No Japanese currency intervention was found as of 11 Nov.
for_you: The yen is weak but steady. A sudden yen surge can unsettle global markets, but none is under way.
rubric_hit: USD/JPY 1w move 0.85% below the 3% Watch line; USD/JPY 1m move 0.87% below the 6% Watch line
why: Cheap yen borrowing funds positions worldwide; a sharp yen rally forces those trades to unwind, as in the global sell-off of August 2024.
drivers: Bank of Japan policy, the US–Japan rate gap, JGB yields, currency intervention, risk appetite.

rubric.alert: A move of more than 5% in a week or 10% in a month, with stress spreading to other markets.
rubric.watch: A 3–5% move in a week, a 6–10% move in a month, or Japanese currency intervention.
rubric.normal: The yen moves less than 3% against the dollar in a week and less than 6% in a month.
